correctness.rationale: The exact spectral decomposition yields eigenvalues \(1-s\) (multiplicity \(k\)), \(1+s\) (multiplicity \(k-1\)), and the two roots of \(\lambda^2-(q+1+s)\lambda+q(1+s-2kt^2)=0\). The positive-definite domain follows from these eigenvalues. For any asymmetric diagonal scale the semidefinite sandwich \(W\preceq A\preceq\kappa W\) can be averaged over graph automorphisms, showing a symmetric scale does at least as well. The scalar condition \(\lambda_+/\min\{\lambda_-,1-s\}\) has a unique minimizer: the crossing \(q_0=s(1-s)/(s-kt^2)\) if \(kt^2\le2s^2/(1+s)\), otherwise \(q=1+s\). The proof also justifies the exact Jacobi locus \(kt^2=s^2\). Exact characteristic-polynomial identities and symbolic crossing identities were verified from the attached standalone code, with 75 spectrum cases, 75 scalar optimizations, and 6000 asymmetric sampling comparisons. Finite experiments are not used to infer global optimality.

value.rationale: The weighted friendship graph is a natural minimal non-bipartite departure from property-A sparsity: \(k\) triangular motifs share a common hub, making diagonal equilibration a meaningful practical baseline. The theorem solves a nontrivial global min-condition-number design problem at arbitrary dimension and identifies two distinct active-eigenmode regimes, a sharp transition in the optimal hub scale, and the exceptional curve on which Jacobi equilibration is truly optimal. It gives an immediately usable closed-form preconditioner in place of an SDP solve and an explicit boundary for a widespread heuristic. This is more than a routine evaluated condition number because it establishes global optimality against asymmetric diagonals and a structural parameter classification.
